# Keyword reference

How each Abaqus keyword is handled. The converter knows the complete CalculiX 2.22 + 2.23 keyword set (**143** cards). Anything in that set is emitted as-is; anything outside it without a translator is commented out with guidance — never silently dropped.

## Translated / converted to an equivalent

| Abaqus keyword | Handling |
| --- | --- |
| `*NODE / *ELEMENT / *NSET / *ELSET` | parsed into the geometry registry and re-emitted canonically (sets resolved, `GEN`→`GENERATE`, gappy ranges pruned). |
| `*NGEN / *NFILL / *NCOPY / *ELGEN / *ELCOPY` | expanded into explicit `*NODE`/`*ELEMENT` (CalculiX has no mesh-generation cards). |
| `*PART / *INSTANCE / *ASSEMBLY` | flattened into one global numbering (instance transform applied, references resolved, names kept ≤80 chars); part-level constraints (`*EQUATION`, `*MPC`, `*RIGID BODY`, `*COUPLING`, ...) copied per instance; a part's `*DISTRIBUTION` gets per-instance names (also where an `*ORIENTATION` or a composite ply names it) and offset element labels; rotated instances rotate `*ORIENTATION` axes (also per-element `*DISTRIBUTION` axes), beam `n1` and `*NORMAL` vectors. |
| `*ORIENTATION` | origin `c` of a 9-value line subtracted from `a`, `b` (ccx has no origin field); `DEFINITION=NODES` resolved to coordinates, `OFFSET TO NODES` commented; `SPHERICAL`→`RECTANGULAR` (warned); rotation line kept. One that names a `*DISTRIBUTION` is preceded by that distribution in ccx's form (see `*DISTRIBUTION`). |
| `*DISTRIBUTION` | per-element orientations, in the form ccx 2.23 runs correctly: each `*ORIENTATION` naming one gets its own copy (ccx gives a distribution to the first only), resolved to one line per element of its solid sections — default line first, origin subtracted, the additional rotation applied to the axes (ccx turns only the first line), a name ccx would read as a number replaced; its shell and membrane sections are split into one plain `*ORIENTATION` + section per direction (ccx gives a shell section the first line). A distribution no `*ORIENTATION` names (shell thickness, material property) is commented. |
| `*DISTRIBUTION TABLE` | dropped for an orientation distribution (ccx needs no table; its lines are always `a, b`); otherwise commented. |
| `*SOLID SECTION` | keeps `ELSET`/`MATERIAL`/`ORIENTATION`; other params dropped; an undefined `MATERIAL` is warned (ccx 2.23 can segfault on it). |
| `*SHELL SECTION` | thickness only (integration-point count dropped); composite plies → one synthesized `*ORIENTATION` per ply angle (S6/S8R only), composed with a base rotation about the normal; `SYMMETRIC` layups mirrored; on continuum shells (SC6R/SC8R, which run as solids) → `*SOLID SECTION` (composite: commented); with a `*DISTRIBUTION` orientation (its own or a ply's) split into one element set, plain `*ORIENTATION` and section per distinct direction. |
| `*SHELL GENERAL SECTION` | → `*SHELL SECTION` (thickness+material form); ABD/stiffness form flagged as unsupported. |
| `*BEAM SECTION` | keeps the supported params; `SECTION=CIRC`: the Abaqus radius becomes ccx's two section diameters (`r` → `2r, 2r`), and 2-node beams under it become 3-node beams with an inserted midside node (ccx 2.23 rejects linear beams with a circular section). `SECTION=PIPE` (outer radius, wall thickness) and `BOX` (`a, b, t1..t4`) data pass through, as both codes read them alike, and `THICK PIPE` → `PIPE`; ccx 2.23 runs these sections only on `B32R`, so their beams become `B32R` (2-node ones with an inserted midside node; see the element reference). |
| `*STEP` | `NAME` dropped; `NLGEOM`, `INC`, `AMPLITUDE=RAMP/STEP` kept; `PERTURBATION` kept only for `*FREQUENCY`/`*BUCKLE` (warned when general steps follow, since its loads then persist); explicit steps get `INC=10000000` + `NLGEOM`; `*END STEP` ensured. |
| `*STATIC` | `RIKS` commented by default (ccx would silently run it as plain static; `--approximate` reframes it); `DIRECT=NO STOP` → `DIRECT`; `STABILIZE` dropped (warned). |
| `*DYNAMIC` | implicit and `EXPLICIT` both native; `DIRECT USER CONTROL` → `DIRECT`; `APPLICATION=QUASI-STATIC/MODERATE DISSIPATION` → `ALPHA=-0.3333` (and `*STEP AMPLITUDE=RAMP` for quasi-static); other Abaqus/Explicit controls dropped. An explicit step in a deck with circular-section beams gets a maximum time increment (4th data field): ccx 2.23 overestimates their stable increment about 1.3-fold (NaN displacements); a fixed `DIRECT` increment above it is warned. |
| `*FREQUENCY` | Abaqus-only params dropped; `EIGENSOLVER=SUBSPACE` max-frequency field blanked (ccx reads it as the lower bound); `NORMALIZATION=DISPLACEMENT` noted (ccx mass-normalizes). |
| `*BUCKLE` | `EIGENSOLVER` dropped; Abaqus range/size fields blanked where ccx reads accuracy/vectors/iterations. |
| `*HEAT TRANSFER` | `END=` / `MXDEM` dropped. |
| `*BOUNDARY` | named types (`ENCASTRE`/`PINNED`/`*SYMM`) expanded to DOFs; `TYPE=VELOCITY`/`ACCELERATION` → a displacement BC whose generated amplitude integrates the history from the DOF's state at the step start (continued in later steps that keep it); DOFs 4-6 dropped on nodes of plane/axisymmetric elements (no rotations there; ccx 2.23 crashes on them). An element end node of a circular-section beam whose rotational BCs hold only some of DOFs 4-6, or a nonzero one, gets a force-free knot beam (elset/material `ABQ2CCX_KNOT`): ccx 2.23 would lock the node's other rotations too. A later step's `OP=NEW`, once shell/beam nodes have had rotational BCs, is dropped when the step re-specifies every BC; where it removes BCs, the shell/beam nodes whose rotations it would break get knot beams too (ccx 2.23 does not rebuild those rotations after `OP=NEW`). On a DOF a rigid constraint also eliminates (ccx stops: dependent side of a MPC and a SPC) the BC is taken off where the reference node's own BCs impose it; identical ones on a `*RIGID BODY` move to its reference node with zero rotations about the other axes, as Abaqus/Standard moves them, where the BC'd nodes hold the same DOFs; the rest is warned (`--approximate` drops it on a kinematic coupling or an `*MPC` and makes the `*RIGID BODY` move, as Abaqus/Standard does). `USER` (Abaqus `DISP`) commented, naming ccx's `uboun.f`. |
| `*DLOAD` | pressures and body loads passed through (`Px` faces match Abaqus); bare `P` on solids flagged; a line without an element set (Abaqus: the whole model) gets a whole-model set; `FOLLOWER=NO` / `CONSTANT RESULTANT` dropped (warned under NLGEOM). Element tractions (`TRVECn`/`TRSHRn`) and beam line loads (`PX`/`PY`/`PZ`/`P1`/`P2` — ccx reads `P1`/`P2` on a beam as a section-face pressure) → consistent nodal forces, as for `*DSLOAD` tractions, and so do `TRVEC`/`TRSHR`/`P` on surface elements (which leave the mesh; `P` is positive along the element normal); gravity on them adds nothing (no mass), other loads on them are commented; user-subroutine labels (`...NU`) commented, naming ccx's `dload.f`. `OP=NEW` keeps the `*DSLOAD` pressures Abaqus keeps (ccx's `OP=NEW` would remove them). |
| `*DSLOAD` | surface pressure → `*DLOAD` with `Px` face labels; surface tractions (`TRVEC`/`TRSHR`, which ccx has no card for) → consistent nodal forces: the face/edge shape functions integrated by Gauss quadrature over the undeformed geometry (times the plane-section thickness, or 2πr on axisymmetric edges; directions normalized and `TRSHR` projected onto the face, as in Abaqus), emitted as a `*CLOAD` (one per amplitude, never `OP=NEW`) at the end of the step. Exact in small-strain steps and, under NLGEOM, for `TRVEC` with `FOLLOWER=NO, CONSTANT RESULTANT=YES`; any other NLGEOM traction is commented (`--approximate` converts it with an `[APPROX]` warning). A pressure on the `SPOS`/`SNEG` side of surface elements (which leave the mesh) → nodal forces too, positive against the surface normal (`SPOS`: the element normal); under NLGEOM only with `--approximate`. On a node with a `*TRANSFORM` the converted forces (also `*DLOAD`'s) are given in its local axes, as ccx and Abaqus read a `*CLOAD` there; a node whose axes are unknown (on the cylinder or polar axis, degenerate, two transforms, a 2-D node turned out of plane) leaves the line commented. |
| `*SURFACE SECTION` | dropped with its surface elements (`SFM3D*`, `SFMAX*`, `SFMGAX*`), which leave the mesh — no stiffness, no ccx element — while their loads become nodal forces; they stay (and ccx stops on them) if `*REBAR LAYER` or `DENSITY=` in a dynamic/frequency step or under gravity gives them physics, unless `--approximate`. |
| `*TIE` | Abaqus-only params (`TYPE=`) stripped; `ADJUST`/`POSITION TOLERANCE` kept. |
| `*MPC` | line by line: `PIN` → `*EQUATION` on DOFs 1-3; `TIE` → per-DOF `*EQUATION` (shell/beam rotations through knots, DOF 11 in thermal steps); `BEAM` → one `*RIGID BODY` per independent node (chained lines one body); `LINK` → linearised `*EQUATION` without `NLGEOM`, ccx `*MPC BEAM` with it (not on beam/shell/plane nodes); `PLANE`/`STRAIGHT` kept; user MPCs and other types commented, line by line. |
| `*CONNECTOR SECTION` | its `CONN3D2`/`CONN2D2` elements (never emitted; ccx has no connector element) become the kinematic constraint of the connection type: `JOIN`, `REVOLUTE`, `ALIGN`, `HINGE` → `*EQUATION`s in the translations and rotation vectors (rotations on a `ROT NODE` or a knot), `*BOUNDARY` lines to ground or a held node (repeated after `OP=NEW`); `BEAM`, `WELD` → `*RIGID BODY` (with the `*MPC BEAM` bodies); `LINK` → as `*MPC LINK`; unconstrained types left out. Under `NLGEOM` only the forms that stay exact (`--approximate`: the rest written linear, `[APPROX]`); a behaviour, other types and explicit-dynamics rotations on beam/shell nodes are commented out with the reason. |
| `*EQUATION` | set-name terms resolved to node numbers, multi-node sets paired in sorted order (as Abaqus does unless `UNSORTED`); terms reordered so the eliminated (first) DOF has no BC and is not eliminated elsewhere; an equation that follows from the others and zero BCs (a duplicate, a loop's closing tie) dropped. |
| `*KINEMATIC COUPLING` | every line kept, as node-surface `*COUPLING` + `*KINEMATIC` per DOF range (the reference node's DOFs 4-6 then take BCs and moments natively); rotation lines on shell/beam nodes become `*EQUATION` ties (see `*COUPLING / *KINEMATIC`). |
| `*COUPLING / *KINEMATIC` | `REF NODE` set → node number; empty `*KINEMATIC` → `1, 3` (a rotations-only card couples nothing); DOFs > 3 clamped; on 2-D nodes `1, 2` (ccx holds their DOF 3 itself). Shell/membrane/beam/truss nodes get a force-free knot beam (elset/material `ABQ2CCX_KNOT`), without which ccx 2.23 rejects the rigid MPC, and the coupled rotations are tied to the reference node's DOFs 4-6 by `*EQUATION`; a shell/beam `REF NODE` turns the coupling into a `*RIGID BODY` whose `ROT NODE` follows it. |
| `*RIGID BODY` | `PIN NSET`/`TIE NSET` → `NSET` (both → their union); `REF NODE` set → node number; an explicit `ROT NODE` is added and BCs/moments on the reference point's DOFs 4-6 move to its DOFs 1-3 (ccx ignores them on the REF NODE); a reference point with a `*TRANSFORM` gives the `ROT NODE` its local axes (warned where they are undefined). Shell/membrane/beam/truss members get knot beams; the rotations of `TIE NSET`/`ELSET` shell/beam members are tied to the `ROT NODE`, `PIN NSET` ones stay free. |
| `*TRANSFORM` | rectangular and cylindrical cards passed through; `TYPE=S` (spherical — ccx has none and reads it as rectangular) commented out and replaced by a rectangular card per node with its spherical axes (1 radial, 3 meridional towards the pole, 2 = 3 × 1, fixed at the original position — exact); nodes on the polar axis keep the global axes (warned). Two cards with different data on a node (Abaqus does not allow it; ccx takes the last) and a 2-D node whose local 3-axis leaves Z (ccx 2.23 gets it wrong) are warned. |
| `*CLOAD` | moments on a rigid-body reference point → its `ROT NODE`; `ORIENTATION=` (local axes) and `FOLLOWER=YES` dropped with a warning; `USER` commented, naming ccx's `cload.f`. |
| `*TEMPERATURE` | passed through (upgraded beams' midside nodes get their end nodes' mean); `USER` (Abaqus `UTEMP`) commented, naming ccx's `utemp.f`. |
| `*FILM / *DFLUX / *CFLUX / *RADIATE` | passed through, except loads from an Abaqus user subroutine (`USER`, a `...NU` label): commented, naming ccx's `film.f` / `dflux.f` / `cflux.f` / `radiate.f` (kept, ccx would run its stock subroutine instead). |
| `*CONTACT PAIR` | missing `TYPE` → `NODE TO SURFACE` (the Abaqus/Standard default; the note suggests `SURFACE TO SURFACE` if ccx struggles to converge); `TIED` → `*TIE`; `SMALL SLIDING` dropped for surface-to-surface; Abaqus-only params dropped. |
| `*SURFACE INTERACTION` | 2D out-of-plane thickness line dropped; `*SURFACE BEHAVIOR, PRESSURE-OVERCLOSURE=HARD` synthesized when missing (the Abaqus default). |
| `*FRICTION` | only `mu` emitted (ccx would read Abaqus' slip-rate / mu_k field as its stick slope); tables / exponential decay / anisotropy warned; `ROUGH` and `mu<=0` dropped. |
| `*PLASTIC` | `HARDENING=JOHNSON COOK` kept (ccx's native law) and given the `*RATE DEPENDENT, TYPE=JOHNSON COOK` card ccx needs to switch it on (C = 0 if the deck has none); `HARDENING=USER` and `DATATYPE=PARAMETERS` commented (ccx would silently skip them); `DEPENDENCIES` collapsed. |
| `*ELASTIC / *DENSITY / *SPECIFIC HEAT / *CONDUCTIVITY / *EXPANSION / *MOHR COULOMB` | `TYPE` token translated (`ORTHOTROPIC`→`ORTHO`, `ANISOTROPIC`→`ANISO`, same constant order); `DEPENDENCIES=n` (field variables, which ccx ignores) collapsed to the Abaqus no-field state, field = 0. A linear-elastic `*ELASTIC` less anisotropic than its material's `*EXPANSION` (isotropic beside `ORTHO`, isotropic / orthotropic / engineering constants beside `ANISO`) is written as `ENGINEERING CONSTANTS` / `ANISO` with the same stiffness, since ccx 2.23 otherwise uses a wrong stiffness in linear steps once the deck has temperatures; temperature rows are added so its stiffness interpolation stays within 1e-4 of Abaqus'. An `*EXPANSION, TYPE=ANISO` whose shear coefficients are zero in every row is written as `TYPE=ORTHO` (the elastic rule then follows `ORTHO`), since ccx 2.23 stops `NLGEOM` steps on any ANISO expansion once the deck has temperatures — unless an orientation or ply angle turns it so that it has shear in global axes. One with shear coefficients gets α12, α13, α23 halved on every row: Abaqus' are engineering (γ12 = α12 ΔT), ccx reads tensor components (ε12 = α12 ΔT). |
| `*HYPERELASTIC` | no model keyword → `POLYNOMIAL` (Abaqus default); `TEST DATA INPUT` commented. |
| `*DEPVAR` | SDV count kept; label lines dropped; `DELETE=` warned (no element deletion in ccx). |
| `*INITIAL CONDITIONS` | `TYPE=STRESS/PLASTIC STRAIN/SOLUTION` expanded per integration point (SOLUTION continuation lines joined by the `*DEPVAR` size); unknown types commented. |
| `*CREEP` | Abaqus `LAW=STRAIN/TIME` → ccx Norton (default, time hardening — warned for strain hardening with m ≠ 0); other laws → `LAW=USER`. |
| `*AMPLITUDE` | keeps `NAME`/`TIME`/`SHIFTX`/`SHIFTY`; `SCALEX`/`SCALEY` applied to the data; `SMOOTH STEP` sampled, `EQUALLY SPACED` expanded, `VALUE=ABSOLUTE` warned, `DEFINITION=USER` (Abaqus `UAMP`) commented, naming ccx's `uamplitude.f`. (`*AMP` alias accepted.) |
| `*RESTART` | keeps `WRITE`/`READ`/`FREQUENCY`/`STEP`; other params dropped. |
| `*SURFACE` | only `NAME`/`TYPE` kept; shell edges `E1..E4` → `S3..S6` (plane elements `S1..S4`); `ANALYTICAL RIGID` / `COMBINE` commented; `SPOS`/`SNEG` flagged; faces of surface elements (not in the ccx mesh) left out, a surface of them only dropped. |
| `*OUTPUT / *NODE OUTPUT / *ELEMENT OUTPUT` | field output → `*NODE FILE`/`*EL FILE` (.frd), history output for a set → `*NODE PRINT`/`*EL PRINT` (.dat); the `*OUTPUT` card is dropped and its `FREQUENCY`/`NUMBER INTERVAL`/`TIME INTERVAL`/`TIME POINTS` go onto the step's first output card (ccx has one for all output of a step: the .frd requests' first, Abaqus' defaults kept; intervals → generated `*TIME POINTS`, or a frequency from a fixed or maximum increment, or in explicit dynamics from ccx's own stable increment, estimated with its Courant formula); `FREQUENCY=0` drops its requests. `VARIABLE=PRESELECT`/`ALL` → the ccx labels of Abaqus' preselected field output for the procedure (see output-reference), plus the variables named under it; preselected history output (energies) is dropped. A step without `*OUTPUT` requests of its own gets the field requests Abaqus carries over written again — at their own frequency, with its procedure's preselected variables, or Abaqus' preselected default where none carries over (ccx would keep the earlier step's cards and frequency); `OP=ADD`/`REPLACE` keeps them beside the step's own. Per .frd variable one node set (ccx keeps the last card's): the whole model before a set, several sets joined; a set the .frd cannot show — beam/shell nodes of a model ccx writes expanded, reference points — is also printed, or gets `OUTPUT=2D` when the deck's .frd output is only U/V/RF. |
| `*NODE FILE / *EL FILE / *NODE PRINT / *EL PRINT` | `POSITION=`/`DIRECTIONS=` stripped, `FREQ`→`FREQUENCY` (one per step, as above), `FREQUENCY=0` dropped, variables mapped and filtered against ccx's label list for that card (an unknown `*EL PRINT` label stops ccx); a print card without a set gets a whole-model set (Abaqus prints everything, ccx nothing). |
| `*CONTACT OUTPUT / *CONTACT FILE` | → `*CONTACT FILE`; `CDISP`/`CSTRESS` kept as ccx's `CDIS`/`CSTR`, other Abaqus contact variables dropped (a card left empty is dropped). |
| `Step data outside a *STEP` | `*CLOAD`, `*DLOAD`, output and procedure cards before the first step (or between steps) are commented — Abaqus rejects them and ccx 2.23 segfaults when the deck has no step. |
| `INPUT= on data cards` | the referenced file's data lines are inlined (ccx reads `INPUT=` only on `*INCLUDE`). |
| `Load audit` | every step the Abaqus deck loads (loads, prescribed values, initial velocities; they persist across steps until `OP=NEW`) must still carry a load after conversion: a step whose loads were all commented out is warned (`Step N is loaded in the Abaqus deck ... but no load survives the conversion`), since ccx would solve it with no load; a deck that loads no step at all is noted. |

## Supported — emitted unchanged

CalculiX accepts these as-is (verified against the ccx 2.22 manual):

`*BASE MOTION`, `*CFD`, `*CHANGE CONTACT TYPE`, `*CHANGE FRICTION`, `*CHANGE MATERIAL`, `*CHANGE PLASTIC`, `*CHANGE SOLID SECTION`, `*CHANGE SURFACE BEHAVIOR`, `*CLEARANCE`, `*COMPLEX FREQUENCY`, `*CONSTRAINT`, `*CONTACT DAMPING`, `*CONTACT PRINT`, `*CONTROLS`, `*CORRELATION LENGTH`, `*COUPLED TEMPERATURE-DISPLACEMENT`, `*CRACK PROPAGATION`, `*CYCLIC HARDENING`, `*CYCLIC SYMMETRY MODEL`, `*DAMPING`, `*DASHPOT`, `*DEFORMATION PLASTICITY`, `*DESIGN RESPONSE`, `*DESIGN VARIABLES`, `*DISTRIBUTING`, `*DISTRIBUTING COUPLING`, `*ELECTRICAL CONDUCTIVITY`, `*ELECTROMAGNETICS`, `*FACE PRINT`, `*FEASIBLE DIRECTION`, `*FLUID CONSTANTS`, `*FLUID SECTION`, `*GAP`, `*GAP CONDUCTANCE`, `*GAP HEAT GENERATION`, `*GEOMETRIC CONSTRAINT`, `*GEOMETRIC TOLERANCES`, `*GREEN`, `*HCF`, `*HEADING`, `*HYPERFOAM`, `*INCLUDE`, `*INITIAL MESH`, `*INITIAL STRAIN INCREASE`, `*MAGNETIC PERMEABILITY`, `*MASS`, `*MASS FLOW`, `*MATERIAL`, `*MATRIX ASSEMBLE`, `*MEMBRANE SECTION`, `*MODAL DAMPING`, `*MODAL DYNAMIC`, `*MODEL CHANGE`, `*NETWORK MPC`, `*NO ANALYSIS`, `*NODAL THICKNESS`, `*NORMAL`, `*OBJECTIVE`, `*PHYSICAL CONSTANTS`, `*PRE-TENSION SECTION`, `*RATE DEPENDENT`, `*REFINE MESH`, `*RETAINED NODAL DOFS`, `*ROBUST DESIGN`, `*SECTION PRINT`, `*SELECT CYCLIC SYMMETRY MODES`, `*SENSITIVITY`, `*SPECIFIC GAS CONSTANT`, `*SPRING`, `*STEADY STATE DYNAMICS`, `*SUBMODEL`, `*SUBSTRUCTURE GENERATE`, `*SUBSTRUCTURE MATRIX OUTPUT`, `*SURFACE BEHAVIOR`, `*TIME POINTS`, `*UNCOUPLED TEMPERATURE-DISPLACEMENT`, `*USER SECTION`, `*VALUES AT INFINITY`, `*VIEWFACTOR`, `*VISCO`

## Passed through with a heads-up

| Keyword | Note |
| --- | --- |
| `*DAMAGE INITIATION` | *DAMAGE INITIATION was added in ccx 2.23 and is emitted unchanged; ccx implements a subset of Abaqus' damage-initiation criteria and has no *DAMAGE EVOLUTION card, so verify your ccx version (>= 2.23), the CRITERION, and that progressive damage is not required to soften/fail the material. |
| `*USER MATERIAL` | *USER MATERIAL kept, but ccx uses its own umat interface (umat_*.f), not an Abaqus UMAT binary — the subroutine must be ported. |
| `*USER ELEMENT` | *USER ELEMENT kept; ensure the matching ccx user-element routine is built in. |

## Same name, different meaning (warned)

| Keyword | Warning |
| --- | --- |
| `*FILTER` | *FILTER in CalculiX is a sensitivity-smoothing card for *SENSITIVITY steps, NOT the Abaqus output filter — emitted as-is but almost certainly wrong; remove it unless this is an optimisation run. |

## Dropped — organisational, no ccx meaning

Silently dropped (with a note): `*ASSEMBLY`, `*END ASSEMBLY`, `*END INSTANCE`, `*END LOAD CASE`, `*END PART`, `*INSTANCE`, `*MANIFEST`, `*PART`, `*PREPRINT`.

Dropped with a warning (can change the model):

| Keyword | Warning |
| --- | --- |
| `*SYSTEM` | *SYSTEM (local coordinate system for following *NODE cards) is unsupported by ccx and was dropped; node coordinates defined under it may be in a rotated frame — verify they are global. |
| `*UNIT SYSTEM` | *UNIT SYSTEM is unsupported by ccx and was dropped (informational only). |

## No CalculiX equivalent — commented out with guidance

Any keyword not in the CalculiX set and without a translator is emitted as `**` comments plus a warning. These have tailored guidance:

| Keyword | Guidance |
| --- | --- |
| `*VISCOELASTIC` | time-domain viscoelasticity is unsupported (ccx *VISCO is a creep STEP, not a material); drop, or approximate with *DAMPING. |
| `*INERTIA RELIEF` | ccx has no inertia relief; constrain with a soft spring-to-ground / 3-2-1 set, or balance with the equilibrating load. |
| `*CONNECTOR BEHAVIOR` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a section that uses it is commented out); remodel as *SPRING / *DASHPOT / *MPC per the behaviour. |
| `*CONNECTOR MOTION` | prescribes motion of connector components, which the converted connector (ccx constraints, no connector element) does not have; the prescribed motion is missing. |
| `*CONNECTOR LOAD` | loads connector components, which the converted connector (ccx constraints, no connector element) does not have; the load is missing. |
| `*GASKET BEHAVIOR` | gasket behaviour has no ccx equivalent. |
| `*COHESIVE SECTION` | ccx has no cohesive element; model debonding with contact (*SURFACE BEHAVIOR) or a nonlinear *SPRING. |
| `*DAMAGE EVOLUTION` | ccx 2.23 added *DAMAGE INITIATION but not *DAMAGE EVOLUTION, so progressive damage cannot fully run (the material will not soften/fail); drop. |
| `*FIELD` | *FIELD predefined fields are unsupported; use *INITIAL CONDITIONS / *TEMPERATURE / *DISTRIBUTION instead. |
| `*REBAR` | rebar/reinforcement layers have no ccx equivalent; mesh reinforcements explicitly. |
| `*BEAM GENERAL SECTION` | no direct ccx card; use *USER ELEMENT (U1) + *BEAM SECTION, SECTION=GENERAL with A, I11, I12, I22, shear factor. |
| `*CONCRETE` | concrete plasticity models are unsupported by ccx; substitute *PLASTIC or remodel. |
| `*CONCRETE DAMAGED PLASTICITY` | unsupported by ccx; substitute *PLASTIC or remodel. |
| `*CONNECTOR ELASTICITY` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR DAMPING` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR STOP` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR LOCK` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR FRICTION` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR PLASTICITY` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR HARDENING` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR DAMAGE INITIATION` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR DAMAGE EVOLUTION` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR CONSTITUTIVE REFERENCE` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR DERIVED COMPONENT` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR POTENTIAL` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR UNIAXIAL BEHAVIOR` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONNECTOR FAILURE` | connector behaviour has no ccx equivalent (a *CONNECTOR SECTION that uses it is commented out). |
| `*CONTACT` | Abaqus general contact has no ccx equivalent; define explicit pairs instead: *CONTACT PAIR, INTERACTION=<name>, TYPE=SURFACE TO SURFACE with two element surfaces (+ *SURFACE INTERACTION / *SURFACE BEHAVIOR). |
| `*CONTACT INCLUSIONS` | general-contact inclusion list (ALL EXTERIOR is not translatable); create the two surfaces and a *CONTACT PAIR instead. |
| `*CONTACT EXCLUSIONS` | general-contact exclusion list; not applicable to ccx *CONTACT PAIR. |
| `*CONTACT PROPERTY ASSIGNMENT` | assigns a general-contact property; in ccx name the *SURFACE INTERACTION via *CONTACT PAIR, INTERACTION= instead. |
| `*LATENT HEAT` | ccx has no *LATENT HEAT; approximate with an apparent *SPECIFIC HEAT peak cp + L/(Tliq-Tsol) over the melting interval. |
| `*EMBEDDED ELEMENT` | no ccx equivalent; mesh the reinforcement conformally or tie the embedded nodes with *EQUATION constraints. |
| `*ALLOWABLE STRESS` | Abaqus 2024 optimisation stress limit; ccx has no equivalent — express a stress constraint via *DESIGN RESPONSE/*CONSTRAINT in a *SENSITIVITY run. |
| `*REDUCED BASIS GENERATE` | Abaqus 2024 reduced-order-basis generation has no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*SUBMODEL CUT` | Abaqus 2024 submodel-cut card; ccx drives submodels with *SUBMODEL plus *BOUNDARY/*CLOAD, SUBMODEL — remodel using those. |
| `*WEAR SURFACE PROPERTIES` | Abaqus 2024 surface-wear properties have no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*ELECTRICAL RESISTIVITY` | ccx parameterises conduction by *ELECTRICAL CONDUCTIVITY (the inverse); convert resistivity -> conductivity. |
| `*ELECTRIC MACHINE LOAD` | Abaqus 2024 electric-machine load has no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*ELECTRIC MACHINE PROPERTY` | Abaqus 2024 electric-machine property has no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*ELEMENT USER OUTPUT VARIABLES` | Abaqus UVARM-style user output; ccx has no equivalent (fill state variables via *DEPVAR + a ccx umat instead). |
| `*PIEZORESISTIVITY` | Abaqus 2024 piezoresistive coupling has no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*STEP CYCLING` | Abaqus 2025 step cycling has no ccx equivalent; remodel as repeated steps. |
| `*STEP CYCLING CONTROL` | Abaqus 2025 step-cycling controls have no ccx equivalent; drop. |
| `*LOAD CASE` | ccx solves one load case per step: the loads of all *LOAD CASE blocks in this step are now SUPERPOSED into one solution — split each load case into its own step (with OP=NEW on the loads). |
